note: status/references describe existing syntactic slices or workflow provenance, not semantic proof. evidence identifies an optional enforcing project-fitness owner for each complete source clause. The 313 ledger entries map to 286 authored clauses: grouped PS entries share one obligation and require proof of the whole group. Missing project evidence remains unverified.

entries.text: Every module is intelligible to a competent engineer who has never seen the repository, given only the module and its public contract. *(Review invariant)*
No understanding of a change requires oral history, a Slack thread, or the presence of the original author. *(ADR & PR governance)*
The bus factor of every critical path is greater than one: a second person can modify it without a guided tour. *(Team governance)*
Every assumption a future reader must not violate is written next to the code that embodies it, not in a separate document that can drift. *(Colocated contracts)*
No identifier requires the reader to know the author's private abbreviation, ticket number, or nickname. *(Enforced: `maintainability/MAINT-NAME-001` & naming review)*
The happy path of every module is readable in one pass, top to bottom, without jumping to a definition to recover intent. *(Layout & structure)*
Every surprise relative to the principle of least astonishment is marked at the point of surprise, with the reason it exists. *(Documented exceptions)*
No comment restates what the code already says; every comment that remains answers a question the code cannot. *(AST slice: `pstack/PS-COMMENT-001`; semantic review remains)*
Deleted explanations are deleted with the code they explained; no comment describes a world the code has left. *(Refactoring hygiene)*
A future reader can answer "what does this do, and what must not change?" from the names and the tests alone. *(Self-describing tests & types)*
Every name denotes a domain concept or an operation, never an implementation accident (`data`, `temp`, `flag`, `obj2`). *(Enforced: `maintainability/MAINT-NAME-001`)*
The ubiquitous language of the domain is the language of the code; a term in the code means the same thing it means to a domain expert. *(Domain modeling)*
Each concept has one name; each name denotes one concept. Synonyms are treated as defects. *(Domain dictionary)*
A rename of a domain concept is atomic across code, tests, and the contract that exposes it. *(Refactoring discipline)*
Boolean names state the true condition (`isClosed`, `hasPendingInvoice`), never a negated or ambiguous predicate. *(Enforced: `maintainability/MAINT-BOOL-001`)*
Units, currencies, and time zones are in the type or the name; a bare number never carries an implicit unit. *(Branded types / naming)*
Abbreviations are expanded unless they are standard in the domain (`HTTP`, `URL`); project-local abbreviations are forbidden. *(Vocabulary review)*
The scope of a name matches its lifetime: a name used across a boundary is stable; a name used inside a function may be short only if its role is obvious in one line. *(Scope hygiene)*

No name encodes a layer, a pattern, or a framework (`UserServiceImpl`, `ManagerHelper`) when a domain name would do. *(AST slice: `maintainability/MAINT-IMPL-001` for Impl/Implementation class names; other pattern names need review)*
A future reader can pronounce every public name and use it in a sentence about the business. *(Spoken clarity)*
The effect of a function is fully described by its name, its arguments, and its declared result; hidden reads and writes of ambient state do not exist. *(Enforced: `pstack/PS-LET-001`)*
No function both answers a question and changes the world. *(Command Query Separation)*
Mutable state does not escape the scope in which a reader can see every write. *(Enforced: `typescript/TS-READONLY-001` & `pstack/PS-LET-001`)*
Control-flow nesting never exceeds two levels; deeper decisions are named functions. *(Enforced: `maintainability/MAINT-NEST-001`)*
A function fits in working memory: one screen, one responsibility, one level of abstraction. *(Enforced: `clean-code/CC-FN-001`)*
Arguments are few enough that the call site reads as a sentence; a long argument list is a missing concept. *(Enforced: `clean-code/CC-FN-002`)*
No Boolean argument selects a hidden second behaviour. *(Enforced: `senior/SR-FLAG-001`)*
Order of statements inside a function is the order of the story; setup, action, and result are not interleaved with unrelated concerns. *(Narrative order)*
A reader can predict the next line. When they cannot, the unpredictability is the defect, not the reader's failure. *(Least surprise)*
Cyclomatic complexity of a function is low enough that every path can be named and tested. *(Branch minimization)*
A requirement change touches one module, or a set of modules whose joint reason to change is explicit. *(High cohesion)*
Shotgun surgery — the same concept edited in many unrelated places — is treated as a design defect, not as normal work. *(Architectural smell)*
What changes together lives together; what changes for different reasons does not share a module. *(Enforced: `architecture/MOD-SHARED-001`)*
A boundary is drawn where the rate of change differs, not where the technology differs. *(Boundary strategy)*
Feature flags and temporary branches have an owner and an expiry; an expired flag is a defect. *(Release engineering)*
No copy of a business rule exists outside its authoritative module. Callers depend on the rule, they do not reimplement it. *(DRY business logic)*
Configuration that operators change is outside the code; configuration that developers change is code, reviewed and versioned. *(12-factor config)*

A database migration is reversible or explicitly marked irreversible, with the recovery path written down before it runs. *(AST slice: `maintainability/MAINT-MIGR-001` for TS/JS migrations without a down step; SQL migrations and reverse correctness need review)*
Public contracts change by addition or by a versioned break; silent changes of meaning are forbidden. *(Semantic versioning)*
The diff of a change is reviewable by a human in one sitting. A diff that cannot be reviewed is two changes. *(Diff atomicity)*
Every module has a public surface small enough to memorise and a private interior free to change. *(AST slice: `architecture/MOD-EDGE-001`; public-surface size is not checked)*
Callers depend on the contract, never on the order of fields, the shape of errors, or the timing of internal calls. *(Encapsulation)*
Third-party types do not leak across a boundary the team owns; an adapter is the only place that knows a vendor. *(Enforced: `architecture/HEX-PORT-001`)*
A boundary documents what it guarantees, what it refuses, and what it leaves undefined. *(Contract specification)*
Error types at a boundary are part of the contract; a new failure mode is a contract change. *(Typed errors)*

Timeouts, retries, and idempotency keys are part of the boundary contract, not an implementation detail discovered in production. *(AST slices: `pstack/PS-IDEM-001` and `vibe-proof/VP-TIMEOUT-001`; retry policy is not checked)*
A module can be deleted. If it cannot, the reason is written on the module, not left implicit. *(Deletability)*
Layering is one-directional. A domain concept does not import a delivery or infrastructure concept. *(AST slices: `architecture/DEP-ENT-001` and `architecture/DEP-UC-001`)*
The dependency graph of the system is acyclic at the module level, or every cycle is named and justified. *(Acyclic dependencies)*
A new team member can draw the boundaries of the system from the repository layout without a diagram that lives elsewhere. *(Screaming architecture)*
The reason for a non-obvious decision sits in an architecture decision record linked from the code it constrains. *(ADR governance)*
ADRs are immutable records; a reversed decision is a new record that supersedes the old one, not an edit of history. *(Immutable decision records)*
Comments explain why, never what. A "what" comment is a failed name. *(AST slice: `pstack/PS-COMMENT-001`; meaning still needs review)*
TODO and FIXME carry an owner and a condition of removal; an ownerless TODO is deleted or promoted to a tracked defect. *(Enforced: `musk/MUSK-REQ-001`)*
No commented-out code remains. History lives in version control. *(Enforced: `pstack/PS-COMMENT-001`)*
The README of a module states its purpose, its non-purpose, and how to run its tests, in under one screen. *(Module documentation)*
Onboarding to a critical path is a written path — build, test, change, observe — not a pairing session that vanishes. *(Written onboarding)*
Runbooks for operational failure live next to the code that fails, or link to it; they are exercised, not merely stored. *(Operability)*
Glossaries of domain terms are generated from the code's public names or checked against them; a glossary that diverges is a defect. *(Glossary sync)*
A future reader can reconstruct the sequence of decisions that produced a module from the record, without interviewing anyone. *(Traceability)*
Tests describe behaviour in the language of the domain, not in the language of the implementation. *(Behavioral tests)*
A failing test names the behaviour that broke, without requiring the reader to open production code first. *(Clear assertions)*
Every behaviour a future editor must preserve has a test that fails if it is lost. *(Living specification)*
Tests do not duplicate production logic; they state examples and boundaries. *(Anti-mirrored test logic)*
A test that fails intermittently is a defect in the test or in the system, and is not ignored. *(Flaky test zero-tolerance)*
Test data is recognisable as domain data. Obscure fixtures (`user1`, `foo`, `xxx`) are forbidden on public behaviour. *(Meaningful fixtures)*
The test suite is the living specification: when the test and the comment disagree, the test is the authority, and the comment is fixed or removed. *(Test supremacy)*
Characterisation tests pin behaviour before a legacy module is changed; unpinned legacy behaviour is not modified. *(Golden master / pinning)*
A test runs in seconds at the unit boundary and does not require a human environment, a secret, or a particular clock. *(Deterministic hermetic tests)*
Deleting a test requires a recorded reason. A deleted test is a deleted promise. *(Enforced: `testing/TDD-DEL-001`)*

Code does not depend on the current date, the author's timezone, or the locale of the machine that builds it, except through an explicit clock and locale port. *(AST slice: `maintainability/MAINT-CLOCK-001` for direct domain clock calls; locale and indirect calls need flow analysis)*
No certificate, key, URL, or vendor endpoint is assumed permanent; each has a rotation or replacement path. *(Secret lifecycle)*

Deprecated surfaces announce their replacement and their removal condition at the point of use. *(AST slice: `maintainability/MAINT-DEPR-001` for empty JSDoc deprecation tags; the stated replacement and removal condition need review)*
A compatibility shim has a deletion criterion written on the shim. *(Enforced: `musk/MUSK-DEL-001`)*
Log lines and error messages remain meaningful after the author has left: they name the operation, the entity, and the failure, not an internal nickname. *(Structured error messages)*
Metrics and traces use stable names. Renaming an observability field is a contract change for the people who page on it. *(Observability stability)*
Data written today can be read by the code of next year, or a migration exists before the write format changes. *(Schema evolution)*
A feature removed from the product is removed from the code. Dead feature paths are not kept "in case." *(Enforced: `musk/MUSK-DEL-001` & dead code removal)*
Dependencies pin versions and record why a major upgrade is blocked; an unexplained pin is a defect. *(Dependency management)*
The oldest code in the repository is still approachable: it meets the same naming and test invariants, or it is isolated behind a boundary marked legacy. *(Legacy quarantine)*
A future editor can run the relevant tests with one command and trust a green result. *(Single-command verification)*
A wrong change fails in the test or at the boundary, not silently in production a week later. *(Shift-left verification)*
Rollback of a release is a documented, practiced path, not a theory. *(Release rollback)*
Feature introduction can be separated from feature activation, so a bad change can be disabled without a redeploy of logic. *(Decoupled release)*
Observability is sufficient for a stranger to tell whether their change worked in production, without asking the author. *(Production telemetery)*
No global mutable singleton is the hidden input of a module a stranger must change. *(Enforced: `pstack/PS-LET-001`)*
Construction of collaborators is visible at the composition root; a stranger can substitute a fake without editing the module. *(Composition root)*
Invariants of a data structure are enforced by the type or by a constructor, not by the hope that every caller remembers them. *(Parse, don't validate)*
Partial failure is explicit. A function does not return success while having done half the work, unless the contract says the operation is partial and how to resume it. *(Explicit failure modes)*
The cost of a mistake on a critical path is bounded: limits, quotas, and kill switches exist before they are needed. *(Blast radius containment)*
Code review checks maintainability for a future stranger, not style preference and not the author's intent as privately understood. *(Maintainability-first review)*
Review comments that encode a real invariant are promoted into code, a test, or an ADR; they do not remain only in the review. *(Promote lessons to structure)*
Ownership of a module is a name a future reader can find. Unowned code is assigned or deleted. *(Named code ownership)*
A module no one can explain is a risk, and is scheduled for characterisation or isolation. *(Risk register)*
Onboarding material is updated in the same change that invalidates it. *(Documentation freshness)*
Commit messages state the problem and the reason, not only the file touched. A future bisect can be read as a narrative. *(Narrative commits)*
Large rewrites are not the plan for unmaintainable code. Incremental characterisation and boundary extraction are. *(Strangler fig refactoring)*
Cleverness that saves lines at the cost of a future reader's hour is rejected. The reader's hour is the scarce resource. *(Clarity over cleverness)*
The team can delete code. Addition without a path to removal is treated as debt. *(Enforced: `musk/MUSK-DEL-001`)*
Every change leaves the touched region easier for the next stranger than it was found, or the reason it could not is written on the change. *(Boy Scout rule)*
Every line of code exists to satisfy a verifiable problem; code with no associated problem is not written. *(Requirement traceability)*
Every fragment of code is intelligible to an engineer who did not author it, without reconstruction of the author's mental context. *(Intelligibility)*
Every non-obvious design decision has a recorded trade-off (ADR) stating context and the rejected alternative. *(ADRs)*
No line of code exists without a justification of value; dead code is deleted. *(Enforced: `senior/SR-DEAD-001`)*
Every third-party dependency is declared, isolated, audited, and replaceable. *(Dependency isolation)*
No known design or code defect remains without an owner and a correction plan. *(Defect ownership)*
The adopted solution is the simplest one that satisfies the current requirement. *(Simplicity principle)*
No abstraction, parameter, or extension exists for a requirement that has not yet been confirmed. *(Enforced: `maintainability/MAINT-EMPTY-001`)*
Each item of system knowledge has exactly one authoritative representation. *(Single source of truth)*
Every module admits a one-sentence explanation containing no exceptional qualifiers. *(Single responsibility)*
The intent of the code is evident to a human reader before it is evident to the compiler. *(Human-readable intent)*
No module is retained out of attachment; it is retained only while it remains the best representation of the problem. *(Objective retention)*
Every corrected defect has an identified root cause, not merely a suppressed symptom. *(Root-cause debugging)*
No unexpected behaviour is left without a verified hypothesis. *(Empirical investigation)*
Every behavioural change is introduced singly, with verification between changes. *(Atomic increments)*
Every communicated estimate is a range with explicit assumptions, never a point value. *(Range estimation)*
Every prototype is discarded or rewritten before it enters production; its only permanent product is learning. *(Throwaway prototypes)*
Every large feature has at least one vertical slice operating end to end before it is widened. *(Workflow invariant; path-shape checks cannot establish an end-to-end running slice)*
No irreversible decision is taken before the information that would make it reversible, or cheap to reverse, is available. *(Reversibility)*
No technology is adopted by fashion; every adoption has a documented criterion of fit to the problem. *(Technology evaluation)*
Every name discloses the intent of the entity without a comment. *(Self-documenting names)*
Every name is pronounceable and searchable across the repository. *(Searchable identifiers)*
Every type bears a noun name; every function bears a verb or verb–noun name. *(Grammatical naming)*
Each domain concept has exactly one term in the code. *(Consistent domain terms)*
No name encodes type, scope, or visibility. *(No Hungarian prefixing)*
No numeric or string literal carrying domain meaning appears outside a named constant. *(Magic literal elimination)*
The entire repository conforms to a single set of formatting rules, enforced by tooling. *(Automated formatters)*
Vertical whitespace separates distinct ideas; visual proximity groups what changes together. *(Visual grouping)*
Every variable is declared in the narrowest scope that permits its use. *(Enforced: `pstack/PS-LET-001`)*
No condition is expressed in negative form when an equivalent positive form exists. *(Enforced: `maintainability/MAINT-BOOL-001`)*
Every function has a single responsibility and a single level of abstraction. *(Single level of abstraction)*
Every function fits on one screen and is comprehensible without scrolling. *(Enforced: `clean-code/CC-FN-001`)*
Every function has at most three arguments, or a single options object if more are required. *(Enforced: `clean-code/CC-FN-002`)*
No function receives a Boolean that selects between two behaviours. *(Enforced: `senior/SR-FLAG-001`)*
Every function is either a command or a query, never both. *(Command Query Separation)*
Every side effect is declared in the function name or in its contract. *(Declared effects)*
No function mutates its arguments unless the contract so declares. *(Argument immutability)*
Every non-trivial conditional branch body is extracted to a named function. *(Branch extraction)*
Every boundary condition is encapsulated in a single place. *(Encapsulated boundary conditions)*
No function has a control-nesting depth greater than two. *(Enforced: `maintainability/MAINT-NEST-001`)*
Every module has exactly one reason to change. *(Single Responsibility Principle)*
Every new case of a known variation is added by extension, without modifying the module that already works. *(Open/Closed Principle)*
Every subtype is substitutable for its base type without altering the observable behaviour of the client. *(Liskov Substitution Principle)*
Every interface exposes only operations that all of its implementers use. *(Interface Segregation Principle)*
Every high-level module depends on abstractions it owns, never on infrastructure concretions. *(Enforced: `architecture/HEX-PORT-001`)*
Every module has high cohesion: its parts change for the same reason. Coupling between modules is explicit and minimal. *(Enforced: `architecture/MOD-SHARED-001`)*
Every “has-a” relation is modelled by composition; inheritance is used only when substitutability holds. *(Composition over inheritance)*
No method navigates more than one level of indirection over objects it did not create, receive, or own. *(Enforced: `senior/SR-CHAIN-001`)*
Every decision that depends on an object's state is taken by that object. *(Tell, don't ask)*
Every point of variation lies behind a stable boundary. *(Protected variation)*
Construction of the object graph is separated from its use. *(Dependency injection / composition root)*
Every dependency is received by constructor or parameter; no module resolves it from a global. *(Explicit dependencies)*
Every domain concept with value equality is immutable. *(Immutable value objects)*
No domain function returns null; absence is an explicit type. *(AST slice: `maintainability/MAINT-NULL-001`; other paths and indirect values need type/flow analysis)*
Every type has a name that a reviewer can speak aloud and understand. *(Pronounceable types)*

Domain, application, infrastructure, and delivery occupy separate boundaries; none imports inward across a boundary. *(AST slices: `architecture/DEP-ENT-001`, `architecture/DEP-UC-001` and `architecture/DEP-IA-001`)*
The domain references neither frameworks, drivers, nor transport protocols. *(AST slice: `architecture/HEX-EDGE-001`; builtin layer checks may cover more when configured)*
Every complex system in production evolved from a simple system that already worked. *(Gall's Law)*
The boundary between modules reflects a real communication boundary of the team, or the discrepancy is documented. *(Conway's Law)*
Every module can be understood, tested, and replaced without reading the interior of its neighbours. *(AST slice: `architecture/MOD-EDGE-001`; understandability is not checked)*
Every published API preserves backward compatibility, or the break is versioned and announced. *(API contract versioning)*
Every invalid state is unrepresentable in the types of the public API. *(Parse, don't validate)*
No secret, environment URL, or feature flag resides in source code. *(AST slices: `vibe-proof/VP-SECRET-001` and `vibe-proof/VP-CLIENT-SECRET-001`; not every URL or flag is detected)*
Every backing service is interchangeable by configuration, without recompilation. *(Pluggable infrastructure)*
No application process stores session state in local memory as the source of truth. *(Stateless processes)*
Every retryable operation is idempotent. *(Enforced: `pstack/PS-IDEM-001`)*
Every call to an external system has a timeout, a bounded retry policy, and a circuit breaker. *(AST slice: `vibe-proof/VP-TIMEOUT-001`; retries and circuit breakers are not checked)*
Failure of one component does not propagate resource exhaustion to its neighbours. *(Bulkheads / fault tolerance)*
Every business operation emits a structured log, metric, or trace sufficient to diagnose it in production. *(Observability)*
The development environment executes the same boundaries and contracts as production, or the difference is isolated and tested. *(Dev/prod parity)*
Every impossible state aborts immediately; no error is swallowed silently. *(Enforced: `clean-code/CC-ER-002`)*
Every failure carries sufficient context to diagnose it without reproducing the case. *(Diagnostic error context)*
The happy path of a module can be read without traversing error handling. *(Separation of errors and logic)*
Every assumption of the form “this cannot happen” is guarded by an assertion. *(Exhaustive switch & assertions)*
Every input that crosses a boundary is validated before use. *(Boundary parsing requires data flow; `pstack/PS-ZOD-001` only constrains validator placement)*
Every process, credential, and role holds only the minimum permissions its function requires. *(Principle of least privilege)*
No secret appears in the repository, in the image, or in the logs. *(AST slice: `vibe-proof/VP-SECRET-001`; images and runtime logs are outside this check)*
No query or command is constructed by concatenating external input. *(Enforced: `vibe-proof/VP-SQL-001`)*
Every ingress boundary verifies authentication and authorisation; none trusts a prior check. *(Zero trust at ingress)*
Every dependency has an update owner and a security-patch policy. *(Vulnerability management)*
Test code satisfies the same naming and structural rules as production code. *(Test code quality)*
Every test asserts a single behaviour. *(Review invariant; assertion presence cannot prove behavioural focus)*
Every test is deterministic, order-independent, and self-evaluating. *(Hermetic testing)*
Every test reads as Arrange–Act–Assert and contains no conditional logic of its own. *(AST slice: `pstack/PS-AAA-001`; helper flow and AAA structure still need review)*
Every corrected defect has a test that failed before the correction. *(Regression tests)*
Every assumption about a library or an external environment is covered by a boundary test. *(Contract testing)*
The test suite passes in full before integration; a broken test blocks the change. *(Pre-commit / CI gate)*
Every third-party adapter has tests that fix the usage contract. *(Adapter integration test)*
The majority of domain behaviours are covered by unit tests; integration and end-to-end tests cover boundaries, not internal logic. *(Test pyramid)*
No test depends on a private implementation detail. *(Public behavior testing)*
No optimisation is merged without a measurement that demonstrates the bottleneck. *(Empirical optimization)*
Every algorithm over unbounded data has known complexity and an explicit bound. *(Algorithmic complexity)*
No mutable state is shared across threads without a demonstrated synchronisation protocol. *(Thread safety)*
No concurrent code exists unless a throughput or latency requirement demands it. *(Simplicity over premature concurrency)*
Every non-deterministic failure is treated as a concurrency or timing defect until shown otherwise. *(Race condition vigilance)*
Every data transformation has explicit input, output, and error policy. *(Pure transformation pipelines)*
Every datum is immutable by default; mutation is local and visible. *(Default immutability)*
Every API that returns or accepts collections has a limit, pagination, or backpressure. *(AST slices: `vibe-proof/VP-FIND-MANY-001` and `vibe-proof/VP-SELECT-001`; other APIs need review)*
Every change is under version control, in a commit whose message explains the why, and does not break the build. *(Conventional commits)*
Every repeatable step of build, test, lint, and deploy is automated; no release depends on an undocumented manual step. *(Automated release engineering)*

**PS-01 (Laziness protocol):** The merged change is the smallest diff that solves the stated problem. Dead code, unused abstractions, and speculative generality are absent. *(Enforced: `maintainability/MAINT-EMPTY-001` & diff minimization)*
**PS-02 (Foundational thinking):** Core types, data structures, and the sharing relation among concurrent actors are fixed before behavioral logic is written.
**PS-03 (Redesign from first principles):** A new requirement is integrated as if it had been a foundational assumption from day one. It is not bolted onto the previous shape.
**PS-04 (Attack the premise):** After two or more fixes that share one premise fail the same gate, the premise is rejected before another patch that assumes it is written.
**PS-05 (Subtract before you add):** Dead weight, redundant validators, and stub references are removed before new structure is built on what remains. *(Enforced: `musk/MUSK-DEL-001`)*

**PS-06 (Minimize reader load):** The number of layers between a question and its answer is minimal. One-caller wrappers are collapsed. Mutable state a reader must hold in their head is absent. *(Enforced: `pstack/PS-LET-001`)*
**PS-07 (Outcome-oriented execution):** A planned rewrite converges on the target architecture. Throwaway compatibility states are not preserved to keep intermediate diffs smooth.
**PS-08 (Experience first):** When implementation convenience conflicts with the consumer’s experience, the consumer wins. Fewer polished capabilities ship in preference to more rough ones.
**PS-09 (Exhaust the design space):** Where no precedent decides the design, two or three competing prototypes are compared before a commitment.
**PS-10 (Build the lever):** Non-trivial edits, migrations, analyses, and checks are performed by a rerunnable tool — codemod, script, generator, or skill — not by unreproducible hand work.
**PS-11 (Model the domain):** A repeated domain rule lives in one structure — a state machine, a typed model, a table — not in scattered conditionals.

**PS-12 (Boundary discipline):** Guards, parsing, and validation sit at system boundaries (CLI, config, network, external APIs). Internal business logic is pure and trusts its types. *(AST slice: `pstack/PS-ZOD-001`; other boundaries need review)*

**PS-13 (Type-system discipline):** Illegal states are unrepresentable. Semantic primitives are branded. External data is parsed at the boundary. Variants are exhaustive. The compiler is not lied to. *(AST slices: `pstack/PS-AS-001` and `pstack/PS-PARTIAL-001`)*
**PS-14 (Idempotent operations):** A retried or partially rerun operation converges to the same end state as a single successful run. *(Enforced: `pstack/PS-IDEM-001`)*

**PS-15 (Migrate callers, then delete):** Callers of a legacy API are migrated and the old API is deleted in the same wave. A compatibility layer is not the resting state. *(Enforced: `pstack/PS-LEGACY-001`)*
**PS-16 (Separate before serializing):** Shared mutable state is eliminated before coordination is added. Serialization is introduced only when a single shared writer is a real invariant.
**PS-17 (Prove it works):** A task is not done until the real artifact has been exercised — the feature run, the value read, the diff inspected.
**PS-18 (Fix root causes):** A defect is reproduced and traced to its cause before code changes. A nil-check or guard whose only effect is to silence the crash is absent.
**PS-19 (Sequence verifiable units):** Multi-step work is broken into units that each end in a checked state. The next unit does not start until the current unit is verified.

**PS-20 (Test behavior, not implementation):** A test calls the code as its user does and asserts an observed value against a literal expectation. *(AST slices: `pstack/PS-WEAK-001` and `pstack/PS-EXPECT-001`; observed behavior needs review)*
**PS-21 (Guard the context window):** Bulk evidence is routed to a subagent. The coordinating thread holds the summary, not the raw payload.
**PS-22 (Never block on the human):** Reversible work proceeds and the result is presented. Confirmation is reserved for irreversible actions.
**PS-23 (Encode lessons in structure):** A lesson that has fired twice is encoded as a lint, a metadata flag, a runtime check, or a script. It is not left as additional prose.
**poteto-mode:** Every non-trivial task is routed through a named playbook. The playbook’s steps are copied into the working list before reasoning begins.
**how:** An explanation of a subsystem is grounded in the code path that implements it, not in recollection.
**why:** A claim about why something was built cites evidence from the record — commits, issues, decision records — not an unsupported assertion.
**recall:** Resumed work rebuilds recent context on the topic from the repository and the session record before new edits start.
**blast-radius:** The safety of a small-looking change is established by executing the code it can affect, not by asserting locality.
**architect:** Types, caller usage, and module shape are settled before code that crosses a function boundary is written.
**arena:** N parallel attempts at the same problem are reduced to one selected result. Competing diffs are not left as the deliverable.
**swarm:** N parallel workers on distinct slices or races produce one aggregated report.
**interrogate:** A diff is attacked by an independent reviewer before it is called done.
**automate-me:** A personal mode skill is drafted from observed working patterns, not from an invented persona.
**make-bot-ui:** A control surface that wakes an agent does so over an explicit webhook contract.
**setup-pstack:** Model assignment per role is written in one rule file. An unstated role keeps its default.
**reflect:** A finished hard task updates the skill or check that would have prevented the miss.
**teach:** A teaching pass leaves the reader able to reconstruct the change.
**tdd:** A bug fix on a cheap local test path has a test that failed before the fix and passes after it.
**no-comments:** Comments that restate the code are absent at review. *(AST slice: `pstack/PS-COMMENT-001`; meaning needs review)*
**typescript-best-practices:** TypeScript edits obey type-system discipline in syntax: no escaped `any`, exhaustive unions, parsed boundaries. *(Enforced: `typescript/TS-ANY-001`)*
**figure-it-out:** When no bundled playbook fits, a rigorous auditable playbook is designed for the task before execution.
**show-me-your-work:** Decisions of a non-trivial task are logged in a reviewable trail a later reader can open.
**create-verification-skill:** A project with no scripted proof of app behavior gains a project-local verify skill before “done” is claimed.
**maintain-verification-skill:** A verify skill whose feature map has drifted from the app is updated from source plus one live pass.
**unslop:** Delivered prose and code contain no filler a maintainer would have to delete to recover the claim.
**bro:** A restatement in plain language preserves the claim and drops the jargon.
**technical-writing:** Docs, RFCs, READMEs, PR descriptions, and commit messages follow a layered standard: claim, evidence, consequence.
**Investigation** is read-only. It answers how, why, or whether, and it does not edit.
**Bug fix** reproduces the defect, names the root cause, and fixes it against runtime evidence.
**Performance** traces a measured slowness and reports the change against a baseline.
**Hill climb** improves one metric against a target by hypotheses with before-and-after measurement.
**Runtime forensics** diagnoses a live symptom from instrumentation, not from a guessed patch.
**Trace forensics** diagnoses a captured profile, trace, spindump, or heap snapshot.
**Feature** builds new or changed behavior from a named data shape.
